description: Gate sequencer of 64 steps, each step carrying a probability, arranged as four rows of 16, two of 32 or one of 64, with a song mode of 64 phrases

params.text: Turns that step's gate on or off and moves the cursor to it; the step is green when its gate is on and yellow while its probability is open, and in song mode it picks a phrase instead
Sets the length of the sequence and its run mode; held for 2 seconds it opens the clock resolution in pulses per step, which is what unlocks the gate types
Splits the 64 steps into four sequences of 16, two of 32, or one of 64
Copies the current sequence, or as much of it as the 4/8/ALL switch chooses, into the buffer; in song mode it copies phrases
Writes the buffer into the current sequence from the cursor, or into the song in song mode
Returns the sequencer to its first step, and puts the write cursor back at the first step
Opens probability for the step at the cursor and puts it on the display, where the main knob sets it from 0 to 1 in steps of 0.02; pressing it again turns that step's probability off
Switches between editing one sequence and building a song out of 64 phrases
Chooses the sequence being played and edited, or in song mode the sequence the phrase under the cursor calls up; it sets the probability instead while one is on the display
Sets how much copy and paste carry: four steps, eight steps, or the whole sequence together with its length and run mode
Chooses the shape of the gate for the step at the cursor; its lamp is green when the clock resolution can produce that shape and red when it cannot

inputs.text: Advances the sequencer one step per pulse; with a clock resolution above one it takes that many pulses for each step
A trigger here returns the sequencer to its first step
A trigger here starts and stops the sequencer
Chooses the sequence from a voltage

outputs.text: The gates of one of the sequences; with four rows of 16 each output carries a row, with two of 32 the first and third carry them, and with one of 64 only the first

notes: pressing copy in one mode and paste in the other runs a shortcut instead: randomizing the gates or the probabilities, clearing the sequence, or refilling the song
in SEQ mode, holding the mouse button down on a step and dragging across the others paints the same gate state onto every step the cursor passes
with the mouse over the sequence display, a sequence number can be typed on the computer keyboard, two key presses within one second reading as a two-digit number
in song mode, with the mouse over the sequence display, the space bar moves on to the next phrase
menu: Lock steps, gates and gate p — stops the steps, the gate type buttons and the gate p button being changed by accident
Reset on run — returns the sequencer to the first step every time it is started
Retrigger gates on reset — holds the gate outputs low for 1ms after a reset so a trigger-sensitive target fires again; the choices are No, Yes, and Only when Run cable is unconnected
Single shot song — plays the song once instead of repeating it
Seq CV in level — sets how the SEQ input is read: 0-10V across the 32 sequences, the note voltages C4-G6, or Trig-Incr, where a trigger steps to the next sequence
AutoSeq when writing via CV inputs — moves on to the next sequence when writing from the expander runs off the end of the current one
Add expander (4HP right side) — places the GS-X expander against the right edge of this module

inputs.0: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.1: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.2: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
